candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 46 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 47 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 48 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 49 not required. 50

candidates.statement: Any modification to drug substance manufacturing carries some risk of causing an adverse 111 impact on quality, either in the physical properties of the drug substance or in the level or nature 112 of impurities present, and, in some cases, to the bioequivalence or safety profile of the drug. 113 Certain kinds of modifications (e.g., equipment or facility changes) are viewed as less likely to 114 result in an adverse impact than others (e.g., changes in the synthetic route). However, each drug 115 substance manufacturer will need to assess the particular modification for their drug substance to 116 determine the risk associated with the change. 14 This guidance applies to changes made 117 throughout the drug substance manufacturing process, i.e., from the starting material through the 118 final drug substance. Late-stage changes in the drug substance manufacturing process are 119 generally viewed as more likely to have an adverse impact on the quality of the drug substance 120 and, consequently, on the drug product. Some late-stage changes should be evaluated not only by 121 comparing pre- and post-modification drug substance, but also by comparing drug product 122 prepared from pre- and post-modification drug substance. Finished drug product manufacturers 123 should ensure that drug substances used in their products meet established specifications and, for 124 compendial drug substances, meet United States Pharmacopeia (USP) standards. 125

A risk assessment should be performed by the drug 130 substance manufacturer to assess the effect of the change, as well as by the drug product 131 manufacturer to evaluate the risks associated with drug substance manufacturing modifications. 132 A reduction in the number of drug substance and/or drug product batches from the 133 recommendations provided in this guidance (see sections VI – XI) may also be acceptable if an 134 adequate justification is provided based on the risk assessment. 135

candidates.statement: After making manufacturing changes, DMF holders or drug substance manufacturers should 211 assess the effects of the changes to the drug substance. 18 A central principle underlying this draft 212 guidance is that a change in the drug substance manufacturing process can be adequately 213 assessed by comparing three consecutive pilot or commercial scale batches of pre- and post- 214 modification material to determine if the quality of the post-modification material is equivalent 215 to or better than the quality of the pre-change material. 19 , 20 Evaluation of the manufacturing 216 change may include but is not limited to: 217
candidates.context: • A comparison of impurities in pre- and post-modification intermediates, the unfinished 219 drug substance, and/or the drug substance. 220 • A comparison of the drug substance’s physical properties before and after modification. 221 • Drug substance stability data. 222

candidates.statement: 19 Whenever possible, changes in site, equipment, or manufacturing process (including changes in the source of the drug substance) should be evaluated using data from commercial-scale batches.

candidates.statement: The impact of manufacturing modifications on the impurity profile (including impurities 234 addressed by ICH M7) is evaluated by determining levels of existing and new impurities. It is 235 important to determine the stage in the manufacturing process at which impurities should be 236 evaluated and to establish the adequacy of the analytical procedures used for this purpose. Levels 237 of residual solvents and inorganic substances should also be considered during evaluation of the 238 impurity profile. 239

The 246 impurity search should also be expanded to include appropriate downstream impurities that may 247 be formed during the manufacturing process. candidates.statement: For some drug products, a change in particle size or shape may affect the content uniformity of 399 the drug product irrespective of the risk that its physicochemical properties or bioavailability 400 could be affected. Content uniformity is more likely to be an issue when the drug substance 401 makes up only a small percentage of the total formulation weight, the drug substance is 402 formulated as a solid, and the drug product is manufactured by a process that can be sensitive to 403 changes in particle size or shape (e.g., dry granulation). If it is likely that the dosage form’s 404 content uniformity will be affected by a change in particle size or shape, and if the drug 405 substance manufacturing change has a high potential to adversely affect the drug substance’s 406 particle size or shape, then comparison of the data from both the drug substance and drug 407 product should be used to evaluate the change. candidates.statement: Scale changes refer to changes in the batch size outside the validated scale for intermediates, the 569 unfinished drug substance, or the drug substance. This section is relevant to scale changes that 570 use the same equipment as listed in the current master batch record (MBR), equipment that 571 differs only in capacity from the equipment listed in the current MBR, or equipment of the same 572 construction material, design, and operating principle as the equipment listed in the current 573 MBR. Changes to equipment with a different construction material or design and operating 574 principle should be considered equipment changes (see section VI.C). Adjustments in process 575 parameters should be limited to those needed to accommodate changes in equipment. In general, 576 scale changes before the final intermediate is produced are less likely to impact the impurity 577 profile or physical characteristics of the final drug substance and less supporting data may be 578 necessary to support the change.
